message.content:
Below is a **complete example** of how you would create a Google Compute Engine instance that has a GPU attached and runs Ubuntu 20.04 LTS.  
(If you’re actually looking for an **AWS EC2** instance, let me know and I’ll give you the corresponding AWS CLI / SDK call.)

---

## 1.  What you’ll need

| Item | Why it’s needed |
|------|-----------------|
| **Project ID** | The GCP project where the instance will live |
| **Zone** | The GCP zone (e.g., `us-central1-a`) |
| **Instance name** | A unique name for the VM |
| **Machine type** | CPU + RAM (e.g., `n1-standard-8`) |
| **GPU type** | NVIDIA GPU (Google offers `nvidia-tesla-a100`, `nvidia-tesla-v100`, etc.) |
| **Image** | Ubuntu 20.04 LTS (`ubuntu-os-cloud/ubuntu-2004-focal-v20230901`) |
| **Service account** | Permissions to create instances & attach GPUs |
| **OAuth token** | For authentication (or use `gcloud auth application-default login`) |

> **NOTE:** Google Cloud does **not** currently offer an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU.  
> The closest equivalent is the **NVIDIA Tesla A100** (`nvidia-tesla-a100`).  
> If you truly need an RTX A6000, you’ll have to use a different provider (e.g., AWS or Azure).

---

## 2.  Using the `gcloud` CLI

```bash
# Set variables
PROJECT_ID="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"
MACHINE_TYPE="n1-standard-8"   # 8 vCPUs, 30 GB RAM
GPU_TYPE="nvidia-tesla-a100"   # closest to RTX A6000
IMAGE_FAMILY="ubuntu-2004-lts"
IMAGE_PROJECT="ubuntu-os-cloud"

# Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
  --project="$PROJECT_ID" \
  --zone="$ZONE" \
  --machine-type="$MACHINE_TYPE" \
  --accelerator=type="$GPU_TYPE",count=1 \
  --image-family="$IMAGE_FAMILY" \
  --image-project="$IMAGE_PROJECT" \
  --boot-disk-size=50GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
  --service-account="default" \
  --scopes="https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform" \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh
```

### Optional: Startup script

Create a `startup.sh` file to install NVIDIA drivers and CUDA:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Install NVIDIA driver
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-470

# Install CUDA Toolkit (example)
wget https://developer.download.nvidia.com/compute/cuda/repos/ubuntu2004/x86_64/cuda-ubuntu2004.pin
sudo mv cuda-ubuntu2004.pin /etc/apt/preferences.d/cuda-repository-pin-600
wget https://developer.download.nvidia.com/compute/cuda/12.2.0/local_installers/cuda-repo-ubuntu2004-12-2-local_12.2.0-1_amd64.deb
sudo dpkg -i cuda-repo-ubuntu2004-12-2-local_12.2.0-1_amd64.deb
sudo apt-key add /var/cuda-repo-ubuntu2004-12-2-local/7fa2af80.pub
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y cuda
```

---

## 3.  Using the REST API

If you prefer to call the Compute Engine REST API directly, here’s a sample `POST` request:

```http
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/instances
Authorization: Bearer {ACCESS_TOKEN}
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "name": "{INSTANCE_NAME}",
  "machineType": "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/machineTypes/{MACHINE_TYPE}",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/{IMAGE_PROJECT}/global/images/family/{IMAGE_FAMILY}",
        "diskSizeGb": 50,
        "diskType": "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        {
          "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT",
          "name": "External NAT"
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "accelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/acceleratorTypes/{GPU_TYPE}"
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": [
        "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\nsudo apt-get update\nsudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-470\n"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Replace the placeholders (`{}`) with your actual values.

---

## 4.  Quick checklist

- [ ] Verify that the GPU type you want is available in the chosen zone.
- [ ] Ensure you have enough quota for GPUs in that zone.
- [ ] Make sure the service account has the `roles/compute.instanceAdmin.v1` role (or equivalent).
- [ ] If you’re using the REST API, obtain an OAuth 2.0 access token (`gcloud auth application-default print-access-token`).

---

### Want to try it out?

1. **Set up the environment**  
   ```bash
   gcloud init
   gcloud auth application-default login
   ```

2. **Run the `gcloud` command** (replace placeholders with your own values).

3. **Verify**  
   ```bash
   gcloud compute instances list --project="$PROJECT_ID" --zone="$ZONE"
   ```

That’s it! You now have a Compute Engine instance running Ubuntu 20.04 LTS with a GPU attached. If you need anything else—like setting up persistent disks, firewall rules, or a custom startup script—just let me know.
